characterization_methods.key_findings: 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-0.4C shows a light grey matrix (austenite) traversed by dark, elongated band-shaped regions aligned with the rolling direction; parts of the grains show a fine lamellar (pearlite-like) constituent, consistent with only partial discontinuous precipitation (Fig. 1(a)).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: through-thickness embedding, grinding and polishing performed separately for hot-rolled and heat-treated samples; all alloys at different processing conditions analysed

characterization_methods.key_findings: In 9Al-10Mn-0.4C a colony of fine, closely spaced bright lamellae/rods nucleates on an almost straight grain boundary decorated with small bright particles and grows into one grain, while the adjacent region remains smooth, dark unreacted austenite; the discontinuous-precipitation product is fine γ + κ-carbide lamellae (Fig. 2(a)).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM analysis performed on selected microstructures
characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (secondary electron imaging, SEI)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Discontinuous precipitation at 600 °C enhanced the hardness of the grades (Table 2, Fig. 1); however no numerical hardness value specific to the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C composition is reported in the paper's hardness tables.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 5 kg load applied for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample; Minitab18 software used to verify data consistency and outliers excluded

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Composition 9Al-10Mn-0.4; temperature axis 0–1300 °C; phases BCC_A2, FCC_A1 (γ), KAPPA_E21.
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD equilibrium phase-fraction calculation (amount of all phases [mol] vs temperature [°C])
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The computed phase-fraction diagram (Fig. 9(a)) shows the austenite (FCC_A1) fraction does not decrease at 800 °C compared with 1150 °C, which the text uses to explain why the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy decomposes at 600 °C (measured, Fig. 1(a)) but not at 800 °C.

interfaces.interface_notes: Discontinuous precipitation starts from the γ/γ grain boundaries, is a reaction involving grain boundary migration, and does not affect the non-transformed parent phase composition. The lamellar product nucleates on an almost straight boundary decorated with small bright particles.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Austenite (γ) evolves through discontinuous precipitation into γ + κ-carbide lamellar structures; in 9Al-10Mn-0.4C at 600 °C the reaction is only partial and starts at the grain boundaries.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Different alloyed steels were produced by casting using a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, resulting in 0.5 kg ingots.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The ingots were hot-rolled at 1150 °C, obtaining 5 mm flat-products, followed by water quenching. This is the parent (hot-rolled, water-quenched) condition of the tempered sample.

Samples were heat treated at 600 °C for 30 min, followed by water quenching; this 600 °C tempering triggered slight/incipient transformations (discontinuous precipitation and precipitation transformation).

grain_structure.texture: banded microstructure aligned with the rolling direction

phases_present.morphology: light grey matrix and dark elongated band-shaped regions; unreacted/non-discontinuous-precipitated austenite
fine, closely spaced bright lamellae/rods forming the discontinuous-precipitation product (γ + κ-carbide lamellae)

precipitates.distribution: nucleated as a colony on an almost straight grain boundary (decorated with small bright particles) and growing into one grain; only partial transformation of the austenite
precipitates.type: κ-carbide lamellae (discontinuous precipitation product, γ + κ fine lamellae)

microstructure_list.region: whole sample (grain-boundary-initiated, growing into grain interiors)

structures.overall_structure: Partial discontinuous precipitation: austenite (γ) matrix, strongly banded and aligned with the rolling direction, with dark elongated band-shaped regions and a fine lamellar γ + κ-carbide constituent in part of the grains; a substantial fraction of unreacted (untransformed) austenite remains.

unmapped_findings: The 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy underwent austenite decomposition (discontinuous precipitation) during tempering at 600 °C (Fig. 1(a)) but NOT at 800 °C, even though kinetics should have been faster at 800 °C; the paper attributes this to the phase volume fraction diagram (Fig. 9(a)), in which the austenite (FCC_A1) fraction along the red line does not decrease at 800 °C compared with 1150 °C.

Boundary conditions proposed as enabling discontinuous precipitation in 9Al-10Mn-0.4C at 600 °C: 10% manganese (Mn and C concentrations not high enough to stabilize the γ phase against its own transformation), the thermal energy introduced at 600 °C, and a lower driving force caused by the lower annealing temperature (600 °C), which allowed grain boundary migration of the forming lamellar phase rather than completing lamellae separation.

No numerical hardness value specific to 9Al-10Mn-0.4C is reported in any hardness table (Tables 2, 4, 5, 8, 9); e.g. Table 2, cited as evidence of the hardening from discontinuous precipitation at 600 °C, gives values only for 9Al-10Mn-1C (273 HV hot-rolled → 439 HV tempered).

Text states the non-transforming behaviour of austenite in the low-C alloy reflects the respective phase volume fraction diagram (Fig. 9(a)): the austenite fraction does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C, which is a qualitative indication of the transformation propensity; alloy hot-rolled conditions before thermal treatment are not identical to those during hot rolling at 1150 °C, so the comparison is indicative and qualitative.
